text.arabic_uthmani: وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغْنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ ۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًۭا ۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۚ وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا۟ فَتَيَٰتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًۭا لِّتَبْتَغُوا۟ عَرَضَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۚ وَمَن يُكْرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ إِكْرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: opening conjunction links this ruling block to the wider legal sequence
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) The small conjunction makes the self-restraint ruling the first beat of a connected legal program: the chain will move through contract, material support, anti-coercion, and divine mercy rather than leaving this as an isolated moral aside.

topics.headline: coordinated legal opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah begin as a connected legal continuation whose first beat will lead into contract, support, prohibition, and mercy.
topics.reason: The initial conjunction is discourse-level: it resumes the legal sequence and opens the first of the ayah’s repeated coordinated beats.

words.gloss_range: lām al-amr turns the next verb into an indirect command
words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l-}}) The command force arrives through a particle: it binds the following restraint verb while keeping the deprived group in third person, before the ayah turns to direct second-person commands and prohibitions for those with social power.

topics.headline: third-person command particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that obligation is imposed on an absent social group before the ayah turns to direct commands for those with power.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as lām al-amr governing the jussive, and the CRITICAL rows add its indirect command force.

words.gloss_range: Form X restraint joins chastity, dignity, and active inward discipline
words.root_gloss_range: restraint, chastity, dignified abstention, and refraining from illicit taking; locally intensified by Form X self-discipline.
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْتَعْفِفِ}} ({{tr:yastaʿfifi}}) Form X makes the action active: the deprived group is told to seek dignified restraint in themselves, not merely to accept exclusion from marriage, until the provision horizon opens.

topics.headline: active self-restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears restraint as an active effort of dignified self-protection, not as passive exclusion from marriage.
topics.reason: The root and Form X rows survive, while the local grammar keeps the sense at self-restraint under command rather than every possible abstention context.

words.gloss_range: plural relative pronoun defines the commanded population by circumstance
words.prose: {{ar:الَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) The relative pronoun does more than point; it forms those who lack marriage access into a legally visible subject of the ruling before their circumstance is specified.

topics.headline: legally visible class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a social class being grammatically formed: those who lack marriage access become the subject of a ruling.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun functions as the subject frame for the following negated finding clause and distributes the rule over the plural group.

words.gloss_range: negation scopes over continued finding rather than a single failed attempt
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) The negation puts absence first: before marriage is named, the clause marks an ongoing inability to find it.

topics.headline: ongoing non-access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the problem is continuing non-access and constraint, not a momentary failure or personal blame.
topics.reason: The particle negates an imperfect verb, so the CRITICAL continuous-negation payoff is locally grammatical.

words.gloss_range: imperfect finding verb keeps marriage availability concrete and ongoing
words.root_gloss_range: finding, encountering, possessing, and sensing; locally narrowed to practical access under negation.
words.prose: {{ar:يَجِدُونَ}} ({{tr:yajidūna}}) The verb portrays continued failure to find access to a marriage path, while its root range leaves open whether the missing element is means, partner, permission, or conditions.

topics.headline: finding as access
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the issue is practical access to a marriage path, with means, partner, and conditions left open.
topics.reason: The broad w-j-d range is narrowed by the object marriage and the legal context to finding or possessing access.

words.gloss_range: indefinite object under negation marks absence of a lawful marriage channel
words.root_gloss_range: marriage, marriage-contract, and sexual union debates; locally the lawful marriage route sought as an object.
words.prose: {{ar:نِكَاحًا}} ({{tr:nikāḥan}}) The indefinite verbal noun makes marriage an unattained social resource; under negation, it reads as no available lawful route, not simply the absence of one named spouse.

topics.headline: any marriage route
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause is about lacking any attainable marriage route, not missing one named spouse.
topics.reason: The contract-versus-consummation debate remains useful, but local syntax makes the word the object of finding in a lawful-marriage frame.

words.gloss_range: endpoint particle prevents restraint from becoming permanent exclusion
words.prose: {{ar:حَتَّى}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}) The endpoint particle turns self-restraint into an interim posture: it stretches only until God enriches from bounty.

topics.headline: bounded waiting horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the restraint command bounded by hoped-for divine enrichment rather than left as an endless deprivation.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive and structurally closes the first beat on divine provision.

words.gloss_range: Form IV enrichment names God as the cause of relief for the deprived group
words.root_gloss_range: wealth, sufficiency, freedom from need, and enrichment; locally Form IV makes God the cause of sufficiency.
words.prose: {{ar:يُغْنِيَهُمُ}} ({{tr:yughniyahumu}}) The Form IV verb makes sufficiency something God causes for the same deprived group; the breadth of enrichment remains open, but the exit from deprivation is tied to divine bounty rather than market success or owner control.

topics.headline: God-caused sufficiency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine enrichment as the exit from deprivation, not market success or owner control alone.
topics.reason: The wealth and sufficiency range survives, while the object suffix and bounty phrase keep it aimed at the group lacking marriage.

words.gloss_range: nominative divine name anchors provision in God’s agency
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, and divine identity; locally the fixed proper name of God in the case required by the clause.
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) The divine name stands as the overt subject of enrichment, so the actor who ends lack is God rather than guardians, owners, or the marriage market; its later case shifts will thread provision, wealth, and mercy through the ayah.

topics.headline: divine subject of enrichment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actor who ends lack is explicitly God, not the social agents named later.
topics.reason: QAC marks the divine name as nominative subject of the enrichment verb, supporting the agency claim.

words.gloss_range: preposition opens the phrase that makes enrichment come from divine bounty
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) The preposition attaches the enrichment to bounty as source or share, closing the first beat with provision coming from God’s surplus.

topics.headline: source-partitive bounty link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the provision as sourced in and drawn from bounty, not as an undefined improvement.
topics.reason: The source and partitive readings both fit the local prepositional tail, so the topic is preserved as a qualified range.

words.gloss_range: possessive bounty names the surplus source of future enrichment
words.root_gloss_range: surplus, bounty, favor, excellence, and virtue; locally divine bounty as the source of enrichment.
words.prose: {{ar:فَضْلِهِ}} ({{tr:faḍlihi}}) Bounty here is possessed by God; the word carries surplus and favor as the source of relief from lack, then echoes the later language of God’s wealth and giving.

topics.headline: divine surplus bounty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that relief from lack is framed as God’s surplus favor, not as bare economic capacity.
topics.reason: The genitive suffix and min phrase support the CRITICAL focus on bounty, surplus, and divine-source formulae.

words.gloss_range: conjunction pivots from waiting restraint to the contract-seeking case
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) This conjunction opens the second beat, moving from those lacking marriage to those seeking a written emancipation contract.

topics.headline: new contract beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move to a new social case without breaking the legal cascade.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the next relative-topic clause and continues the same coordinated architecture.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun topicalizes people seeking the writing
words.prose: {{ar:الَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) The relative pronoun creates the contract-seeker class before any owner-facing command appears, preparing the imperative that will answer them through a plural suffix chain.

topics.headline: contract-seeker class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees another legally defined group appear before the owner-facing imperative answers it.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is topicalized and answered by the later imperative, matching the CRITICAL structural claim.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII seeking begins a root arc later inverted by prostitution and profit seeking
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, desiring, overreaching, transgression, and prostitution; locally differentiated by each grammatical frame.
words.prose: {{ar:يَبْتَغُونَ}} ({{tr:yabtaghūna}}) Here the seeking is legitimate and contractual, aimed at legal freedom; the same root will later turn darker in prostitution and in the exploiters’ worldly-gain seeking.

topics.headline: legitimate seeking against corrupt seeking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one b-gh-y movement seeks legal freedom while later uses expose exploitation and greed.
topics.reason: The broad root range is narrowed by the object contract here, while intra-ayah recurrence preserves the contrast with later b-gh-y words.

words.gloss_range: definite writing is narrowed to the mukātaba contract and answered by the cognate imperative
words.root_gloss_range: writing, prescribing, recording, and contractual fixing; locally the manumission contract and its imperative answer.
words.prose: {{ar:الْكِتَابَ}} ({{tr:al-kitāba}}) The definite writing is the requested manumission contract, not scripture in general, and the next command repeats the root as an action: write the agreement with them.

topics.headline: specific manumission writing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the object is not scripture in general but the technical writing of a freedom contract.
topics.reason: Local object position after seeking and the cognate imperative support the mukātaba reading; broader book/scripture branches are blocked locally.

words.gloss_range: contracted preposition and relative frame the seekers through the ownership formula
words.prose: {{ar:مِمَّا}} ({{tr:mimmā}}) The fused particle begins the ownership-source phrase, using property grammar for persons just before their request triggers a route out through contract-writing.

topics.headline: property-grammar source class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the tension that persons are introduced through property grammar just before the text commands a route out.
topics.reason: The local phrase is min plus mā before the possession formula, preserving the CRITICAL tension without changing referent identity.

words.gloss_range: perfect possession verb names the existing control that the contract command will transform
words.root_gloss_range: possession, control, ownership, and sovereignty; locally the ownership formula put under emancipation pressure.
words.prose: {{ar:مَلَكَتْ}} ({{tr:malakat}}) The perfect verb belongs to the ownership formula, but the surrounding syntax moves that ownership toward legal release rather than leaving it static.

topics.headline: ownership formula under pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ownership acknowledged only to be pressed toward emancipation duty.
topics.reason: The possession-root range is limited by the formula and the feminine agreement with the following plural, while the emancipation pressure survives.

words.gloss_range: plural right hands with your suffix make power and possession explicit
words.root_gloss_range: right side, right hand, oath, and auspicious power; locally a metonym for possessive control.
words.prose: {{ar:أَيْمَانُكُمْ}} ({{tr:aymānukum}}) The phrase makes possession a second-person domain: your right hands mark the owners’ control before the contract command makes those same addressees write and give.

topics.headline: right-hand possession metonymy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the owners’ control is grammatically named before the command makes them write and give.
topics.reason: The hand/oath range is narrowed locally to the established right-hand possession formula, with possessive power foregrounded.

words.gloss_range: fa links the relative topic to its legal answer
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) The hinge particle ties the defined class to the imperative response: once the seekers are named, the command follows.

topics.headline: topic-to-command hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the contract-seekers’ request move directly into an owner-facing command.
topics.reason: The particle functions as the apodosis or predicate connector after topicalization, so the command does not float separately.

words.gloss_range: Form III imperative with object suffix makes contract-writing a legal speech-act toward them
words.root_gloss_range: writing, prescribing, recording, and contractual fixing; locally the manumission contract and its imperative answer.
words.prose: {{ar:كَاتِبُوهُمْ}} ({{tr:kātibūhum}}) The imperative answers the requested writing as a commanded written transaction, not mere sympathy; Form III makes the contract relational, and the object suffix keeps the seekers directly present.

topics.headline: write the mutual contract
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees emancipation not as sentiment but as a commanded written transaction involving the seekers themselves.
topics.reason: The imperative and Form III mutual-contract morphology survive, while juristic force is kept at the level of a locally commanded legal act.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle qualifies the imperative by known good
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) The condition particle restrains the contract command so it is gated by assessment, not arbitrary refusal or automatic procedure, sending the reader forward to what the addressees know in the seekers.

topics.headline: condition on the contract command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the contract command is not arbitrary; it is gated by an assessment meant to prevent abuse.
topics.reason: The conditional force is clear, but the exact juristic scope is left qualified by the following knowledge-and-good phrase.

words.gloss_range: second-person perfect makes owners responsible for recognized good
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, recognizing, ascertaining, and marking; locally achieved judgment used as a legal condition.
words.prose: {{ar:عَلِمْتُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalimtum}}) The verb makes gatekeeping an accountable act of ascertained knowledge from the addressees, not vague suspicion: they must have recognized good in them.

topics.headline: ascertained knowledge gate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the condition demands ascertainment from those addressed, not vague suspicion.
topics.reason: The perfect verb and object phrase support achieved knowledge, while the kind of knowledge is supplied by the khayr phrase rather than specified here alone.

words.gloss_range: preposition and suffix place the criterion inside the contract seekers
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:fīhim}}) The prepositional phrase locates the good in the contract seekers themselves, making the condition about their own capacity or integrity rather than owner preference alone.

topics.headline: good located in them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that agency and worth are returned to the seekers themselves rather than kept in owner preference.
topics.reason: The fī phrase locally attaches to good as an internal quality in the plural referents.

words.gloss_range: khayr remains broad enough to include moral and practical fitness
words.root_gloss_range: goodness, benefit, moral worth, and suitability; locally an indefinite criterion inside the contract condition.
words.prose: {{ar:خَيْرًا}} ({{tr:khayran}}) The indefinite good is deliberately capacious: moral reliability, practical capacity, and benefit can all sit inside the condition, so the legal criterion is not reduced to one financial test.

topics.headline: indefinite good criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the legal criterion as positive and open-ended, not reduced to a single financial test.
topics.reason: The indefinite accusative object supports breadth, while local contract context narrows it to relevant fitness for the agreement.

words.gloss_range: conjunction expands contract duty into financial support
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) This conjunction adds a second command to the first: contract-writing is joined to material support.

topics.headline: second imperative added
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that writing the contract is not enough; the ayah adds giving as a coordinated obligation.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the next imperative with the writing command, preserving the double-duty structure.

words.gloss_range: imperative giving mirrors God’s prior giving to the addressees
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, giving, and causing to come; locally Form IV means giving or granting.
words.prose: {{ar:آتُوهُمْ}} ({{tr:ātūhum}}) The command says give them, keeping the contract seekers as direct recipients; the later matching verb will make the reason explicit, because the addressees themselves were first given by God.

topics.headline: give from what was given
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees human redistribution grounded in divine prior grant: give them because you were given.
topics.reason: The imperative with object suffix and the later perfect echo support the reciprocal giving payoff.

words.gloss_range: min makes the gift come from a share of God’s wealth
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) The preposition turns giving into transfer from a source or share, preparing the phrase that names the wealth as God’s and recasting the addressees as stewards rather than absolute owners.

topics.headline: partitive stewardship source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressees are stewards distributing from a divine resource, not absolute owners donating from themselves.
topics.reason: Source and partitive senses both fit the phrase, and both support the stewardship force before God’s wealth.

words.gloss_range: singular construct wealth recasts property as belonging to God
words.root_gloss_range: wealth, property, and resources; locally singular construct wealth assigned to God.
words.prose: {{ar:مَالِ}} ({{tr:māli}}) The construct noun makes wealth God’s wealth, so the economic command is grounded in divine ownership rather than the owners’ discretionary charity.

topics.headline: God’s wealth not private hoard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the economic command grounded in divine ownership rather than in the owners’ discretionary charity.
topics.reason: The construct with the divine name makes God the possessor, and the singular noun keeps wealth as a theological category.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name completes the construct and reframes property relation
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, and divine identity; locally the fixed proper name of God in the case required by the clause.
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) The genitive divine name completes the phrase: the wealth belongs to God, so the God who enriches in the first beat is also named as owner of the wealth now redistributed.

topics.headline: divine possessor of wealth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that God is named not only as giver of future enrichment but as owner of the wealth now redistributed.
topics.reason: The divine name is genitive as the possessor in the construct phrase, matching the CRITICAL property-relation claim.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun shifts God’s wealth into a reminder of God’s action toward you
words.prose: {{ar:الَّذِي}} ({{tr:alladhī}}) The relative pronoun keeps the wealth in view while opening the clause that says God gave it to you.

topics.headline: relative tail on wealth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the command’s rationale move from ownership to prior divine giving.
topics.reason: The pronoun modifies the wealth phrase and introduces the following perfect verb as its explanatory tail.

words.gloss_range: perfect giving makes human giving answer God’s completed gift to them
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, giving, and causing to come; locally Form IV means giving or granting.
words.prose: {{ar:آتَاكُمْ}} ({{tr:ātākum}}) The perfect verb grounds the imperative in a completed prior gift: what they are ordered to give to the seekers came to them first from God.

topics.headline: prior divine gift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the economic loop: what they are ordered to give came to them first from God.
topics.reason: The Form IV perfect mirrors the earlier giving imperative and takes the addressees as object.

words.gloss_range: conjunction opens the coercion beat after contract and support duties
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) This conjunction begins the prohibition beat, shifting from write and give to do not coerce.

topics.headline: pivot to prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah turn from positive commands to a direct block on exploitation.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the prohibitive clause and continues the coordinated legal sequence.

words.gloss_range: lā al-nāhiya governs the jussive and blocks coercive agency
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) The prohibitive particle reverses the earlier command mode: where lām ordered restraint, this lā blocks coercion.

topics.headline: prohibitive negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a legal stop-sign before the coercion verb: the act is prohibited, not merely criticized.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as prohibitive governing the jussive, supporting the CRITICAL contrast with command lām.

words.gloss_range: Form IV k-r-h turns dislike into forced action and begins the coercion chain
words.root_gloss_range: aversion, dislike, compulsion, and coercive causation; locally Form IV names forced action and its aftermath.
words.prose: {{ar:تُكْرِهُوا}} ({{tr:tukrihū}}) The Form IV verb names causative coercion: do not make them undergo what they resist, and the same root will recur as condition and aftermath.

topics.headline: causing aversion as coercion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees coercion as making another person undergo what they resist, a root chain that returns in the closing condition.
topics.reason: The aversion root range is narrowed by Form IV causative grammar and the object, while broader compulsion parallels remain supporting context.

words.gloss_range: possessive plural names the vulnerable women inside the prohibition
words.root_gloss_range: youth, young servant status, and juridical response through the fatwā field; locally the vulnerable women named as objects of coercion.
words.prose: {{ar:فَتَيَاتِكُمْ}} ({{tr:fatayātikum}}) The word humanizes the direct object of the ban as your young women under the addressees’ control, enclosing them in the coercion frame while refusing to let them disappear into property language.

topics.headline: young women made explicit objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the victims are not abstract; the word marks young women under the addressees’ control as the direct object.
topics.reason: The youth and status associations survive, while local object position and possessive suffix keep the referent tied to the coercion prohibition.

words.gloss_range: preposition marks coercion pressed onto the named act
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) The preposition gives the coercion a direction: pressure is placed onto the named practice that follows.

topics.headline: imposition vector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the spatial force of imposition: the women are being forced onto a target activity.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following prostitution noun and functions as the vector of coercion.

words.gloss_range: definite verbal noun narrows b-gh-y to prostitution and forms the center of the root contrast
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, desiring, overreaching, transgression, and prostitution; locally differentiated by each grammatical frame.
words.prose: {{ar:الْبِغَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-bighāʾi}}) The definite verbal noun names prostitution, not generic seeking; it darkens the same root that earlier marked contract-seeking and stands before the later profit-seeking verb.

topics.headline: named prostitution within b-gh-y arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same seeking root darken into the named institution of prostitution before returning as profit-seeking.
topics.reason: Local governance by ʿalā and the definite verbal noun support prostitution, while broader b-gh-y seeking remains as contrast.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle introduces the women’s desire clause without weakening the ban
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) The condition draws attention to the women’s stated desire for chastity and protection; it intensifies the violation while guarded interpretation blocks any inference that coercion is permitted when such desire is not stated.

topics.headline: condition foregrounding will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condition highlights their will for chastity while guarded interpretation blocks permission to coerce otherwise.
topics.reason: The conditional form is preserved, but CRITICAL and guardrail reasoning keep it from becoming a loophole in the prohibition.

words.gloss_range: third feminine plural verb gives the women explicit verbal agency
words.root_gloss_range: wanting, willing, seeking, and aiming; locally the women’s stated desire for self-protection.
words.prose: {{ar:أَرَدْنَ}} ({{tr:aradna}}) The verb gives the women their own clause of will as feminine plural subjects: they wanted self-protection before the purpose clause exposes the exploiters’ profit motive.

topics.headline: women’s will stated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the women as subjects of willing before the text exposes the men’s profit motive.
topics.reason: The verb is 3fp perfect with the women as subject and the following verbal noun as object.

words.gloss_range: Form V fortress root makes chastity active protection
words.root_gloss_range: fortress, protection, chastity, and guarded status; locally Form V self-fortification.
words.prose: {{ar:تَحَصُّنًا}} ({{tr:taḥaṣṣunan}}) The verbal noun makes their desired chastity feel like self-fortification: a protective stance set directly against coercion and profit-seeking.

topics.headline: self-fortification as chastity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears chastity as self-fortification, a protective desire set against coercion and profit.
topics.reason: The fortress-root image and Form V reflexive force survive, while local object position keeps the selected sense at chastity or self-protection.

words.gloss_range: purpose particle governs the exploiters’ seeking and contrasts the opening command lām
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li-}}) This lām is not a command but a motive marker, exposing why the coercion happens: the addressees seek worldly goods, not lawful need or divine command.

topics.headline: purpose lām exposes motive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the coercion happens: not need or law, but the addressees’ purpose of gaining worldly goods.
topics.reason: The particle is lām al-taʿlīl governing the subjunctive, and its contrast with word 2 is structurally explicit.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII seeking repeats the earlier legal seeking with inverted agency and motive
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, desiring, overreaching, transgression, and prostitution; locally differentiated by each grammatical frame.
words.prose: {{ar:تَبْتَغُوا}} ({{tr:tabtaghū}}) The verb completes the seeking reversal: the enslaved sought a freedom contract, while the coercers now seek worldly gain through coercion.

topics.headline: corrupt seeking of gain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root reversal: the enslaved seek a contract, while exploiters seek worldly gain through coercion.
topics.reason: The b-gh-y recurrence survives as an intra-ayah arc, but local object and purpose lām select profit-seeking here.

words.gloss_range: construct noun marks the sought profit as passing worldly goods
words.root_gloss_range: display, exposure, passing goods, accident, and offer; locally fleeting worldly gain as the object sought.
words.prose: {{ar:عَرَضَ}} ({{tr:ʿaraḍa}}) The object names the profit as passing goods, setting a transient target against the stable language of God’s wealth and bounty earlier in the ayah.

topics.headline: fleeting gain object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the exploiters’ target as transient gain rather than stable benefit or divine bounty.
topics.reason: The object position and construct formula support worldly gain, while the broader display/accident range is kept as evaluative pressure.

words.gloss_range: middle construct noun keeps the gain tied to a particular life, not life absolutely
words.root_gloss_range: life, living, vitality, and related modesty associations; locally life qualified by the nearer/lower adjective.
words.prose: {{ar:الْحَيَاةِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥayāti}}) The word life is grammatically suspended inside the construct, so the profit is not from life in its fullest sense but from the life immediately qualified as lower and nearer.

topics.headline: life qualified by lowness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the profit is not from life in the fullest sense but from the lower-world life qualified by the next word.
topics.reason: The construct chain makes life the middle term of the formula, while the following adjective supplies the local qualification.

words.gloss_range: dunyā qualifies life as the nearer/lower world and judges the gain’s horizon
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, and the nearer life; locally a qualifying adjective for worldly life.
words.prose: {{ar:الدُّنْيَا}} ({{tr:al-dunyā}}) The adjective marks the gain as lower and nearer, reducing the coercers’ motive to the small horizon of worldly life over against divine bounty and mercy.

topics.headline: nearer lower-world horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coercers’ profit reduced to the lower, nearer horizon over against divine bounty and mercy.
topics.reason: The comparative-root pressure survives as evaluative color, while local grammar makes it an adjective of life in the fixed formula.

words.gloss_range: conjunction resumes the coercion case and opens the mercy consequence clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) This final conjunction opens the last beat, carrying the coercion case toward consequence and divine mercy.

topics.headline: final consequence beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from prohibition into the theological aftermath of violation.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the final man-conditional and completes the repeated wa-beat structure.

words.gloss_range: conditional man catches any coercer and expects the fa-marked answer
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) The conditional whoever universalizes the perpetrator beyond the owners already named; any coercer is caught, and the clause then waits for the answer naming God’s forgiving mercy.

topics.headline: whoever universalizes perpetrator
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final ruling is not limited to the owners previously named; any coercer is caught.
topics.reason: The conditional particle governs the jussive protasis and is open in reference, supporting universality.

words.gloss_range: coercion verb repeats k-r-h and fuses the feminine plural object to the act
words.root_gloss_range: aversion, dislike, compulsion, and coercive causation; locally Form IV names forced action and its aftermath.
words.prose: {{ar:يُكْرِهْهُنَّ}} ({{tr:yukrihhunna}}) The verb restates the banned act in conditional form, with the feminine plural suffix carrying the coerced women inside the word itself rather than leaving them implied offstage.

topics.headline: victims carried in the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coerced women grammatically carried inside the conditional verb, not implied offstage.
topics.reason: The jussive Form IV verb has the 3fp object suffix and repeats the earlier prohibited root.

words.gloss_range: fa binds the coercion condition to the emphatic divine response
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) The answer particle pulls the condition into its response: the mercy clause is syntactically tied to whoever coerces them rather than floating as a general formula.

topics.headline: answer particle to mercy clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mercy clause is syntactically tied to the coercion case rather than floating as a general formula.
topics.reason: The particle marks the apodosis of the man-conditional and combines with inna for emphatic consequence.

words.gloss_range: inna makes the closing divine predicates certain and grammatically anchored
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) The emphatic particle anchors the final nominal sentence, making God’s forgiveness and mercy after coercion a firm assertion rather than a tentative wish.

topics.headline: emphatic mercy assertion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ending as a firm assertion of forgiveness and mercy after coercion, not a tentative wish.
topics.reason: The particle governs the divine name as accusative subject and the two attributes as predicates.

words.gloss_range: accusative divine name anchors absolution in God rather than the coercer
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, and divine identity; locally the fixed proper name of God in the case required by the clause.
words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهَ}} ({{tr:allāha}}) The accusative divine name is the subject of the closing predicates, so the God named in enrichment and wealth now becomes the agent of mercy rather than leaving absolution to the coercer.

topics.headline: God as mercy agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same divine name from provision and wealth now become the subject of mercy.
topics.reason: The divine name is ism inna and the CRITICAL case-chain rows connect its roles across the verse.

words.gloss_range: min begins the phrase that locates mercy after coercion
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) The preposition starts the temporal tail: from after their coercion, the mercy statement is located in the aftermath and keeps the violation in view.

topics.headline: afterward temporal start
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that mercy is framed from the aftermath of violation, keeping the harm in view.
topics.reason: The preposition combines with baʿd in a temporal phrase modifying the closing attributes.

words.gloss_range: baʿd makes post-coercion time a grammatical construct
words.root_gloss_range: distance, afterwardness, and separation; locally temporal aftermath after coercion.
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْدِ}} ({{tr:baʿdi}}) The word after turns distance into time, making the post-coercion condition a named grammatical space.

topics.headline: aftermath named as space
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the aftermath itself named as the place where divine mercy is asserted.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by min and governs the coercion verbal noun, building the temporal construct.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun with feminine suffix names their coercion as suffered duress
words.root_gloss_range: aversion, dislike, compulsion, and coercive causation; locally Form IV names forced action and its aftermath.
words.prose: {{ar:إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ}} ({{tr:ikrāhihinna}}) The root chain ends as a noun: their coercion, with the suffix marking the women as victims rather than agents while the mercy close answers that legal aftermath.

topics.headline: coercion nominalized for victims
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the act transformed into a legal aftermath belonging to the women as victims, not agents.
topics.reason: The Form IV verbal noun and objective suffix support victim-directed coercion; the variant is kept as reinforcing evidence, not the governing parse.

words.gloss_range: first predicate presents abundant covering-forgiveness directed to the coerced aftermath
words.root_gloss_range: covering, forgiving, shielding, and pardoning; locally the first divine predicate after coercion.
words.prose: {{ar:غَفُورٌ}} ({{tr:ghafūrun}}) The first predicate names God as abundantly forgiving after coercion; its covering sense turns toward removing blame and restoring those whose agency was overridden, not excusing the coercer.

topics.headline: forgiving after coercion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close turns toward removing blame and covering harm for the coerced women, not excusing the coercer.
topics.reason: The predicate is intensive and objectless, so the nearest coherent referent and CRITICAL rows narrow the mercy toward the coerced women.

words.gloss_range: second intensive predicate leaves the legal cascade on restorative mercy
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, compassion, womb-related care, and restoration; locally the closing divine predicate.
words.prose: {{ar:رَحِيمٌ}} ({{tr:raḥīmun}}) The final word adds settled mercy to forgiveness, closing the five-beat legal sequence with compassion and bodily restoration after exploitation rather than on coercion or worldly gain.

topics.headline: mercy closes the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word complete the ayah with compassion, bodily restoration, and theological closure after exploitation.
topics.reason: The faʿīl attribute and mercy-root field survive, while local syntax keeps it as the second predicate paired with forgiveness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وليستعفف الذين لا يجدون نكاحا حتى يغنيهم الله من فضله
baseline_models.mechanism: Practical inability to attain marriage starts a bounded interval of active self-restraint, not passive exclusion; the interval points toward a sufficiency that can make lawful relation possible.

activation_trace.role: Withholding oneself from what is improper makes the waiting period an active discipline.
Capacity, means, and wealth make not finding marriage legible as practical inability as well as failed attainment.
The marriage-contract image identifies the unavailable lawful relation toward which the interval is ordered.
The wealth-and-marriage branch lets enrichment name provision that enables marriage, not cash in isolation.
Grace as benefaction supplies the expected source of changed capacity.

changed_reading.before: A bare command to suppress desire because marriage is unavailable.
changed_reading.after: A temporally bounded discipline under scarcity whose promised horizon is marriage-enabling sufficiency from divine benefaction.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: والذين يبتغون الكتاب مما ملكت أيمانكم فكاتبوهم إن علمتم فيهم خيرا
baseline_models.mechanism: The owned person's seeking initiates a formal route out of ownership: the holder must recognize viable good and answer the request by making the emancipation contract.

activation_trace.role: Seeking gives the contract requester directional agency within the ayah's threefold pattern of pursuits.
The specific manumission-contract branch turns writing into an enforceable path toward release.
Possession and disposal name the asymmetrical relation that the requested contract is meant to alter.
The right-hand image fixes the conventional possession construction while keeping embodied control visible.
Known or disclosed capacity supplies the stated assessment gate.
Useful good or fitness is what the holder is commanded to recognize in the requester.

changed_reading.before: An owner may optionally reward a compliant dependent.
changed_reading.after: A dependent's own request activates a commanded contractual exit from ownership, conditioned on recognizable viability rather than ownerly whim.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم
baseline_models.mechanism: The same giving root links the command to transfer resources to the prior fact that the holders themselves received them; calling the asset God's wealth makes the payment a return-flow of trust.

activation_trace.role: Giving names both the downstream command and the upstream divine gift, joining source and recipient in one transfer circuit.
Acquired and accumulated property is the material being redirected.
The explicit divine name identifies the wealth's prior owner and source rather than treating it as autonomous private stock.
Benefaction supplies the wider logic in which received provision becomes provision for another.

changed_reading.before: The holder adds a charitable gift from private property to a freedom contract.
changed_reading.after: Entrusted divine provision must circulate into the freedom process because the present holder is a recipient before being a giver.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يبتغون الكتاب ... إن أردن تحصنا ... لتبتغوا عرض الحياة الدنيا
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah stages a collision of directions: dependents seek a freedom contract, women will self-fortification, and coercers seek a worldly commodity. The prohibition blocks the powerful party from converting another person's will and body into its own gain.

activation_trace.role: Seeking links the request for contract and the coercer's pursuit of gain while exposing their opposed objects.
The prostitution branch names the sexual channel through which the coercive pursuit operates.
Will and intention give the women an expressly stated direction toward protection.
Protected sexual integrity supplies the object of their stated will.
Forcing another to do what she rejects identifies the mechanism that overrides that will.
Worldly merchandise, substitute, or payoff identifies the coercer's object as commodified gain.
The near or lower world constrains the gain to an immediate horizon.

changed_reading.before: A discrete ban on one immoral occupation.
changed_reading.after: A map of conflicting agencies in which power is forbidden to overwrite a subordinate's freedom-seeking or self-protective will for near-term profit.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ومن يكرههن فإن الله من بعد إكراههن غفور رحيم
baseline_models.mechanism: The close repeats coercion, marks an after, and opens covering and mercy there. It keeps the violation named while establishing an aftermath not exhausted by the coercer's act; the grammatical beneficiary remains open.

activation_trace.role: Repeated compelled action keeps coercion, rather than the women's conduct alone, as the causal event.
Temporal afterness creates a distinct post-coercion horizon.
Covering the fault and protecting its bearer from consequence opens a restorative reading of forgiveness.
Tender mercy supplies care in the aftermath rather than a denial that harm occurred.

changed_reading.before: A generic forgiving formula that closes and potentially erases the offense.
changed_reading.after: A marked post-coercion zone in which the violation remains causally explicit and divine covering and care interrupt its effects, without settling the mercy's referent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding ayah first commands the community to marry off the unmarried, explicitly refuses poverty as a terminal bar, and repeats enrichment from divine grace. Focus-ayah restraint therefore reads as the residual interval after a positive facilitation duty, not the community's substitute for it.

activation_trace.role: Causing marriage for another places a prior affirmative duty on the addressed community.
Need and lack of means name the obstacle the preceding command refuses to make final.
The wealth-and-marriage branch repeats marriage-enabling enrichment immediately before the focus.
Divine benefaction is the repeated source for overcoming poverty.
Self-restraint remains the focus response during whatever inability persists.

structural_cues: 24:32 immediately precedes 24:33 and moves from a plural marry-off command through poverty and enrichment to those who still do not find marriage.
The same ن ك ح, غ ن ي, الله, and فضل sequence crosses the ayah boundary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, the causative community command, poverty, and the repeated enrichment formula. I infer an order of responsibility in which facilitation is attempted before restraint bears the remaining interval. A live alternative is that the two ayat give parallel duties without establishing procedural priority.

changed_reading.before: People lacking marriage bear an isolated duty to wait chastely.
changed_reading.after: Their restraint is a fallback within a social program that first obliges others to facilitate marriage and not treat poverty as disqualifying.

context_deltas.mechanism: The accusation sequence distinguishes good presumption and disclosed knowledge from unsupported speech, while repeating that God knows where people do not. That discipline sharpens the contract criterion into accountable recognition of evidence of good or viability, not an unreviewable character veto.

activation_trace.role: Thinking useful good of fellow believers supplies a positive presumption rather than default suspicion.
Judgment after an indication contributes an evidentiary rather than arbitrary mode of assessment.
The absence of disclosed knowledge condemns claims passed onward without epistemic warrant.
The contrast between divine knowing and human not-knowing limits confidence in human gatekeeping.
The focus criterion requires something actually recognized or disclosed in the requester.
Good as benefit or fitness specifies the positive object to be recognized.

structural_cues: 24:11-19 repeatedly tests accusation, presumption, speech without knowledge, and the asymmetry between divine and human knowing.
خير appears in both the demanded good presumption at 24:12 and the manumission assessment at 24:33.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated epistemic policing and the خير/علم echoes. I infer that the holder's assessment must be evidence-responsive and cannot function as a prejudicial escape hatch. A live alternative is that 24:33 grants a narrower prudential assessment unrelated to the accusation discourse.

changed_reading.before: The owner may deny contracting whenever the requester fails a subjective goodness test.
changed_reading.after: The criterion is an accountable recognition of demonstrable good or capacity under a surah-wide warning against suspicion and claims without knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier rules protect women marked by sexual inviolability from verbal accusation unless knowledge-bearing testimony is produced, and later declare the accused cleared of what is said. When the focus names women who desire self-fortification but are coerced, the context blocks abuse from being converted into their reputational guilt.

activation_trace.role: Casting an accusation by speech identifies the secondary reputational attack controlled by the surah.
Sexual inviolability names the protected status of the accused women.
Testimony as statement grounded in knowledge sets an evidentiary barrier against transferred blame.
Clearance and separation from an allegation provide the discourse's exonerating endpoint.
The coerced women's own will toward sexual protection anchors continuity with the protected status.
Compulsion assigns the causal override to the coercing party.

structural_cues: 24:4 and 24:23 repeat accusation against محصنات; 24:33 reuses the same حصن field in the women's own desire for تحصن.
The early pericope makes speech, proof, and exoneration central consequences of sexual allegations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared حصن field, accusation rules, proof, exoneration, and explicit coercion. I infer that coerced conduct cannot erase the women's claimed inviolability or license reputational guilt. A live alternative is that the accusation rules regulate separate cases and do not directly adjudicate the aftermath of prostitution.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition stops forced prostitution but leaves the coerced women's social status unstated.
changed_reading.after: The surah's proof regime protects their self-claimed sexual integrity from being overwritten by the abuse or by accusations built from it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier warning condemns making conspicuous indecency spread; the focus later exposes an economic mechanism that can manufacture and circulate it. Responsibility shifts upstream from the exploited woman's visible act to the coercer who produces it for gain.

activation_trace.role: Diffusion and public spread supply the social propagation mechanism.
Flagrant transgression beyond proper limits names what is made to circulate.
Prostitution supplies the specific sexual practice generated in the focus.
Compulsion identifies the upstream production mechanism rather than free participation.
Worldly merchandise or payoff identifies the incentive sustaining that mechanism.

structural_cues: 24:19 describes a desire that indecency spread among believers; 24:33 describes a desire for worldly proceeds achieved by forcing prostitution.
Both passages distinguish an agent's desired outcome from the people through whom it is made visible.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies spread, flagrant indecency, coercion, prostitution, and profit-seeking. I infer a causal arrow from commercial coercion to the social production of indecency. A live alternative is that فاحشة in 24:19 primarily names scandalous allegation rather than the coerced practice itself.

changed_reading.before: Forced prostitution is one individual's private sexual offense.
changed_reading.after: It is also an upstream economic infrastructure for producing and spreading the very indecency the surah condemns, so culpability tracks the coercive producer.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across houses, sight, sexual openings, and the movements of owned dependents, access is bounded by permission and refusal has operative force. The focus prohibition extends that architecture to sexual and economic agency: possession does not authorize entry through another person's bodily will.

activation_trace.role: Explicit authorization is required before crossing a domestic boundary.
Returning when told to return makes refusal behaviorally effective.
Guarding inviolability and chastity extends boundary duty to the sexual body.
The bodily opening between the legs locates a protected intimate boundary.
Owned dependents themselves participate in a request-and-permission procedure around privacy.
The same possession relation is shown operating under procedural limits.
The repeated right-hand possession phrase ties those limits directly to the focus population.
The women's expressed will supplies the intimate decision that must remain theirs.
Coercion is the prohibited crossing that makes permission meaningless.

structural_cues: 24:27-31 moves from house entry to gaze and sexual privacy; 24:58 returns to permission for those under right-hand possession.
At 24:28 a denied entrant must turn back, giving another party's refusal practical force.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated permission, effective refusal, bodily guarding, and the same possession class. I infer one boundary architecture extending from domestic space to sexual agency. A live alternative is that house etiquette and bodily coercion are legally distinct even if their spatial logic resonates.

changed_reading.before: Ownership is limited by a narrow ban on compelling one commercial sex act.
changed_reading.after: The ban belongs to a broader permission regime in which house, gaze, body, and dependent agency remain bounded against unconsented access.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated grace refrains culminate in people of grace and means being told to give, while divine increase and apportioned provision remain open-ended. The focus payment into manumission becomes one concrete conduit in a surah-wide circulation of received abundance.

activation_trace.role: Benefaction characterizes the people whose resources generate a duty toward others.
Breadth of wealth and livelihood names material capacity to give.
Giving carries that capacity toward vulnerable recipients.
Increase and growth keep provision from being imagined as a closed stock depleted by transfer.
Apportioned gift identifies divine provision as the continuing upstream source.
The repeated give/gave construction installs manumission funding inside that flow.
Accumulated wealth is the stock the command opens toward the requester.

structural_cues: فضل الله ورحمة recur at 24:10, 24:14, and 24:20 before 24:22 commands giving by people of فضل and سعة.
24:38 again joins increase from فضل with provision without ordinary reckoning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated grace, capacity, giving, increase, and provision. I infer a common circulation logic whose focus-ayah outlet is funding release. A live alternative is that the several recipient classes and legal forms remain discrete despite sharing a theology of provision.

changed_reading.before: The manumission payment is an isolated concession attached to one contract.
changed_reading.after: It is a specified outlet of a recurring economic ethic: abundance received as grace must move toward vulnerable people and freedom.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's human possession sits inside the later declaration of God's sovereignty over the whole cosmos and the closing declaration that all it contains belongs to God. Human control is therefore delegated and accountable, which explains why it is bounded by contract, transfer, privacy, and noncoercion.

activation_trace.role: Sovereignty and kingship locate ultimate dominion with God rather than the local holder.
Human possession recurs as a limited social relation subject to privacy rules.
The right hand as power makes the holder's practical force visible precisely where rules constrain it.
The divine name anchors the closing claim that everything in heaven and earth belongs upstream.
The local possession relation is the one ordered to open a contractual path out.
Naming God's wealth and God's mercy places both assets and judgment above the holder.

structural_cues: 24:42 states God's ملك of heavens and earth; 24:64 closes with everything in both belonging to God and being known by God.
Between those declarations, 24:58 regulates the same ملكت أيمانكم class through privacy obligations.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies nested uses of ملك, the all-belongs-to-God frame, and concrete limits on human possession. I infer delegated stewardship rather than absolute property. A live alternative is that divine sovereignty and human legal ownership operate at different levels without altering the latter's formal category.

changed_reading.before: The owner exercises absolute private dominion softened by selected duties.
changed_reading.after: The holder exercises a subordinate, answerable custody whose built-in limits include recognizing agency, financing release, and forbidding coercive profit.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later mirage sequence moves from calculated appearance, through arrival, to finding nothing and then full accounting. It supplies a temporal model for the focus's near-world commodity: coercive proceeds look attainable now but dissolve at the point of true finding and reckoning.

activation_trace.role: A water-like gleam with no water supplies the deceptive gain image.
Supposition names the thirsty person's initial valuation of the apparent asset.
Counting and accounting reverse that supposition at settlement.
Finding first fails with the sought object and then succeeds before God, pivoting appearance into encounter.
Full payment without deficiency supplies the final reckoning mechanism.
A passing occurrence that soon vanishes makes worldly proceeds intrinsically unstable.
Worldly merchandise or substitute identifies the apparent asset being pursued.
Seeking supplies the coercer's motion toward that apparent asset.

structural_cues: 24:39 uses حتى إذا, failed finding, and حساب; 24:33 uses حتى for deferred sufficiency and calls coercive profit عرض الحياة الدنيا.
The focus root وجد reappears twice at the mirage's moment of collapse and encounter.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies transient worldly merchandise, seeking, mirage, failed finding, and full accounting. I infer that the mirage sequence models the trajectory of coercive gain. A live alternative is that 24:39 concerns unbelieving works generally and does not single out the focus transaction.

changed_reading.before: Worldly proceeds are a real benefit weighed against a moral prohibition.
changed_reading.after: The coercer's supposed asset is already marked as passing and, under the mirage sequence, proves a failed find that terminates in exact accounting.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier sequence joins wrongdoing's aftermath to explicit repair before the same forgiving-merciful close. That pattern keeps the focus formula from functioning as automatic impunity for coercers, while leaving divine covering readily oriented toward those acted upon.

activation_trace.role: Repair as the opposite of corruption supplies a substantive condition in the earlier mercy sequence.
The earlier after marks a transition whose changed conduct includes repair.
Forgiveness follows the explicit repentance-and-repair structure there.
Mercy completes that conditioned restoration pattern.
Coercion remains the named wrongdoing whose perpetrator cannot silently disappear into the close.
The repeated after invites comparison between the two aftermath structures.
Forgiveness opens after coercion without itself specifying an effortless pardon for the coercer.
Mercy preserves a restorative horizon for those harmed.

structural_cues: 24:5 has تابوا من بعد ذلك وأصلحوا followed by فإن الله غفور رحيم; 24:33 has من بعد إكراههن followed by the same divine pair.
The focus repeats coercion three times before the mercy close, preserving causal attribution.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prior repentance-repair-after-mercy syntax and the focus's coercion-after-mercy syntax. I infer that wrongdoer-directed forgiveness cannot bypass repair, while victim-directed mercy remains live. A live alternative is that the repeated formulae have different referents and no carried condition.

changed_reading.before: The closing divine names may be taken as immediate absolution of whoever coerced the women.
changed_reading.after: The surah's earlier repair grammar resists cheap impunity: mercy after coercion can restore the coerced, while a coercer's pardon remains inseparable from repentance and repair.

context_deltas.mechanism: Near the surah's end, the same self-restraint stem is explicitly called better for women who no longer expect marriage. This echo preserves the focus's temporary scarcity function while adding a coexisting reading of self-restraint as chosen protective good, not merely frustrated waiting.

activation_trace.role: The repeated self-withholding stem names an affirmative option in a different marriage horizon.
Useful good explicitly evaluates that restraint positively.
No expectation of marriage separates the positive value from a merely temporary route to marriage.
The focus command anchors the echo in the same discipline.
Its until-enrichment horizon preserves the focus audience's distinct temporary and marriage-enabling structure.

structural_cues: 24:60 repeats يستعفف and خير while explicitly describing women who do not expect نكاح.
24:33 and 24:60 address different audiences and temporal horizons, so the echo adds rather than collapses their functions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the same stem, an explicit خير judgment, and contrasting marriage horizons. I infer that restraint can be intrinsically chosen good as well as temporary scarcity management. A live alternative is that the legal situations are too distinct for 24:60 to revise the motivation in 24:33.

changed_reading.before: Self-restraint matters only as a temporary deprivation until marriage becomes affordable.
changed_reading.after: It remains temporary in the focus sequence but also participates in a positively valued agency of self-protection that need not derive all meaning from eventual marriage.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the small-remnant sense of ع ف ف and the water-channel sense of ء ت ي are remote concrete branches, not suitable lexical translations here. It remains anchored by the focus's own convergence of little remainder, surplus, wealth, and repeated giving; downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for scarcity and redistribution.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يستعفف ... من فضله ... وآتوهم من مال الله الذي آتاكم

activation_trace.role: A small remainder, including milk left after an earlier milking, turns the restraint root into an image of living on constrained residue.
Increase and what remains after need or division supplies the corresponding surplus held elsewhere.
A channel that lets water reach its basin supplies a concrete routing image for the repeated give/gave circuit.
Accumulated property identifies what can be opened from surplus toward the person living with little.

changed_reading.before: Restraint is private management of sexual desire, and the later payment is a separate charity rule.
changed_reading.after: As a contained scarcity image, one person subsists on a remainder while another holds surplus received upstream; the ayah orders a channel between them, so restraint cannot justify withholding material support.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's non-dominant ف ت ي mapping to ف و ت, especially unilateral action without consultation, rather than the ordinary young-woman or enslaved-woman sense. The mapping is packet-authorized and converges tightly with إرادة, coercion, and the surah's permission procedures; render it as a secondary sound-and-branch activation, never as the noun's direct gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ولا تكرهوا فتياتكم ... إن أردن تحصنا

activation_trace.role: Preempting another's matter without consultation supplies a latent indictment of unilateral control around the noun itself.
Expressed will supplies the consultation-relevant direction being overridden.
Forcing another to do what she rejects realizes unilateral action at maximum intensity.
The later authorization procedure keeps subordinate requests and permissions socially operative.

changed_reading.before: فتياتكم only identifies the vulnerable population subjected to the prohibition.
changed_reading.after: As a carefully qualified alternate-root activation, the word also sounds an internal warning against preempting those women's own decision without authorization or consultation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain spatial-optical reading is surprising and must not turn the light parable into a lexical gloss of تحصن. It remains anchored in the حصن branch's protected enclosure and in the packet's niche, transparent vessel, light, and raised house sequence; downstream prose should mark it as imagery for protected agency, not a final interpretation.

activation_trace.role: A guarded interior within an encircling fort supplies the focus's spatial anchor.
The lamp niche supplies an interior whose enclosure houses rather than extinguishes radiance.
The transparent glass vessel models protection compatible with visibility and agency.
Illumination identifies what the protected interior preserves and amplifies.
Dwelling and shelter extend the protected-interior image into inhabited social space.

changed_reading.before: The women's desired fortification is withdrawal into a mute defensive wall.
changed_reading.after: As a contained image, self-fortification is a protected interior that keeps their own light and agency intact; coercion is a breach of that enabling enclosure, not liberation from it.

strongest_changes: The adjacency of 24:32 makes individual restraint a residual interval after communal marriage facilitation and refusal to let poverty decide the case.
The house, gaze, body, and permission sequence turns the anti-coercion clause into part of a broad boundary architecture that recognizes subordinate agency.
Repeated grace, giving, provision, and God's cosmic ownership recast wealth and human possession as accountable trusts that must fund release rather than exploitation.
The accusation and repair sequences preserve coerced women's protected status and prevent the mercy close from becoming cheap impunity for coercers.
The mirage and accounting sequence exposes profit from coercion as a passing apparent asset rather than a durable benefit.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet repeatedly reactivated the focus's own roots across different systems: نكاح/غنى/فضل in facilitation, حصن/عفف/خير in protected agency, ملك/يمين in bounded possession, علم in evidentiary discipline, and غفر/رحم in repair. Spatial permission, economic circulation, and the mirage sequence changed the focus without displacing its words.
remaining_uncertainties: The syntax leaves materially live questions about the scope of إن أردن تحصنا and whether the final forgiveness is oriented to the coerced women, repentant coercers, or both.
خير in the contract criterion may denote moral character, practical earning capacity, trustworthy performance, or a wider beneficial fitness; the packet does not force one.
The permission, mirage, remainder, alternate-root, and fortified-light models are analogical activations, not claims that the context supplies direct lexical substitutions.
The sequencing supports communal responsibility before individual restraint, but it does not fully specify which actors must supply marriage costs or how the duty is institutionally enforced.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A binding inscription becomes an instrument of release.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ك ت ب` B001 is joining/fastening, B003 an inscribed binding determination, and B005 the slave's manumission contract; `م ل ك` B002 is ownership/disposal; `ء ت ي` B002 is granting; `م و ل` B001 is possessed wealth. **Structural cue:** the ayah orders owners to contract with those seeking release and then to give them from the wealth already given by God; 24:28-32 have linked authorized access, restraint, and household capacity, while 24:34-38 move toward clarifying signs, light, and provision. **Assigned role:** writing binds the terms firmly enough to transform ownership, and transferred wealth makes performance possible. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies ownership, a formal bond, payment, and release-oriented contract; I infer constraint made explicit → accountable performance → exit from status. **Reading change:** writing is paradoxically liberative here: a transparent, enforceable bond creates a path out of a coercive relation.

2. **One root exposes the asymmetry between legitimate seeking and exploitative pursuit.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ب غ ي` B001 is seeking (`يبتغون`, `لتبتغوا`), B003 overstepping into oppression, and B005 sexual exploitation (`البغاء`); `ك ر ه` B003 is coercing another into what is disliked; `ح ص ن` B002 is guarded sexuality. **Structural cue:** dependents first seek a contract for themselves, but owners later seek transient worldly goods by overriding women's stated wish for guardedness. **Assigned role:** the repeated root puts two pursuits on one axis while coercion marks the directional imbalance between them. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies self-directed seeking, owner-directed gain, refusal, and force; I infer that pursuit becomes oppression when one agent converts another's body and will into merchandise. **Reading change:** the ayah distinguishes agency-producing desire from desire that consumes another's agency, rather than condemning “seeking” in general.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:34-35 unexpectedly gave the release contract an optical frame: clarified signs and protected light made transparent, ordered mediation the opposite of coercive hidden control. 24:38's surplus provision then reinforced the commanded material enablement.

baseline.text: Evlenme imkânı bulamayanlar, Allah onları lütfundan zenginleştirinceye kadar iffetlerini korusunlar. Elinizin altında bulunanlardan yazılı anlaşma isteyenlerle, kendilerinde bir iyilik görürseniz anlaşma yapın. Allah'ın size verdiği maldan onlara da verin. İffetli kalmak isteyen sahip olduğunuz genç kadınları dünya hayatının geçici çıkarını elde etmek için fuhşa zorlamayın. Kim onları zorlarsa, zorlanmalarından sonra Allah çok bağışlayan, çok merhamet edendir.

findings.text: İffeti koruma, bugünkü imkânsızlıkla ilerideki yeterlik arasındaki dönemi zorlamadan geçiren etkin bir bekleme disiplinidir.
Yazılı sözleşme burada bağlayıcılığı köleliği kalıcılaştırmak için değil, şartları görünür ve uygulanabilir kılarak mülkiyet ilişkisinden çıkış yolu açmak için kullanır.
Aynı arama kökü, kişinin özgürlük sözleşmesi istemesiyle sahibin başkasının iradesini geçici kazanca çevirmesi arasındaki farkı açar: arayış, başka birinin bedenini araç yaptığında baskıya dönüşür.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Marriage Converts Lack into Household Capacity
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Marriage is a transition from unpaired status toward a protected household, mediated by resources, sufficiency, and restraint during delay.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sufficiency branches explicitly treat marriage itself as enrichment and fortification, while patient delay appears as a controlled temporal operation rather than passive exclusion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: From Unpaired Status to Contracted Pair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person lacking a spouse is actively brought into a recognized marital bond.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: interruption of spousal pairing `quranic:root_000073:B001/m01`; causing another to enter marriage `quranic:root_001548:B003/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001548:B002/m01`; acquisition of marital affiliation `quranic:root_001548:B004/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The unpaired state is not treated as an essence. A communal causative act and a legal bond convert it into affiliation. The operation distributes responsibility beyond the prospective spouses alone.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Marriage Converts Lack into Household Capacity

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Poverty Becomes Sufficiency
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Material need is met by an enlarging gift that makes a household viable, with marriage itself functioning as a form of sufficiency.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: material poverty and need `quranic:root_001169:B002/m01`; material independence `quranic:root_001110:B001/m01`; functional sufficiency `quranic:root_001110:B002/m01`; marriage as enrichment and protection `quranic:root_001110:B006/m01`; breadth of means `quranic:root_001647:B003/m01`; unowed divine gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `إِن يَكُونُوا فُقَرَاءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ`; 24:33 `حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Enrichment is not reducible to cash accumulation. It includes enough function, widened capacity, and the stabilizing relation created by marriage. The sequence reframes economic lack as a condition that can be transformed rather than a permanent bar.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Restrained Waiting
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person unable to reach marriage holds desire within a guarded boundary until capacity changes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: restraining oneself from what is improper `quranic:root_001031:B001/m01`; guarded sexual integrity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`; gentle pacing and delay `quranic:root_000610:B005/m01`; practical easing of hardship `quranic:root_001647:B005/m01`; useful good sought in the interim `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ`; 24:33 `وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ ... إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Waiting is an active containment scene with a specified terminus, not indefinite suspension. Restraint protects the sexual boundary while gradual easing and recognized good prepare a changed material state.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Dependent Status Can Be Written Toward Release or Forced Toward Exploitation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Power over dependents takes opposite procedural forms: a written, funded route out of ownership or coercive conversion of another's body into worldly return.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Writing branches assemble, inscribe, bind, and finally emancipate; coercion branches instead override aversion and turn sexual violation into an extractive transaction.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Emancipation Contract
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Separated terms are joined into writing, made binding, and directed toward release from owned status.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: joining parts into one construction `quranic:root_001283:B001/m01`; inscribed document `quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`; binding legal determination `quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`; manumission contract for staged payment `quranic:root_001283:B005/m01`; owned human status `quranic:root_001444:B002/m01`; enslaved person opposed to the free `quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`; enslaved youth or servant `quranic:root_001130:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَائِكُمْ`; 24:33 `يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The four writing senses form a procedural sequence: assemble terms, record them, give them binding force, and orient performance toward freedom. The contract is therefore a machine for changing status, not merely a document about it.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Capital Transfers Capacity
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The party holding resources transfers part of that capacity so the dependent can perform the release agreement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: accumulated property `quranic:root_001457:B001/m01`; giving and delivery `quranic:root_000009:B002/m01`; unowed material gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`; generosity as a gift-bearing quality `quranic:root_000452:B005/m01`; beneficial good recognized in another `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:33 `إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا وَآتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي آتَاكُمْ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Contract alone cannot alter status if all capacity remains with the owner. Granting money redistributes the means of performance and makes the written route materially traversable. The verse locates the owner's capital inside a prior chain of giving.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Coerced Sexual Extraction
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A controller overrides another's aversion, presses her toward prostitution, and seeks a worldly return from the forced act.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: natural or moral aversion `quranic:root_001295:B001/m01`; forcing another to do what she rejects `quranic:root_001295:B003/m01`; aggressive transgression `quranic:root_000138:B003/m01`; prostitution and sexual exploitation `quranic:root_000138:B005/m01`; pressuring another's will `quranic:root_000610:B002/m01`; worldly commodity or compensating return `quranic:root_001001:B008/m01`; protective chastity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:33 `وَلَا تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا لِّتَبْتَغُوا عَرَضَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: This is the inverse of funded release. The controlling party extracts value by defeating another's will and protective boundary. Keeping aversion, coercion, sexual transgression, and worldly return distinct reveals the full transaction rather than hiding it inside a broad category of immorality.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın biçimlerdeki sakınma ve özdenetim çekirdeğini korur; yasak olandan uzak durma ve birini bir şeyden alıkoyma gibi yapıya bağlı kullanımları bu çekirdekle karıştırmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyden ve özellikle memeden kalan az miktarı temel alır; ayrıca ilk sağımdan sonra yeniden sağma ile bir şeyi azar azar alma kullanımlarını açıkça bildirir. Mevcut dal bu farklı gerçekleşmeleri tek bir az kalıntı çevresinde toplarken onları birbirine indirgemez.
